chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqub ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) seeking his counsel regarding marriage, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Marry, and let it be with one who is of Religion, may your hands be enriched.'

key_terms.تَرِبَتْ يَدَاكَ: May your hands be enriched/prosperous (a blessing for sustenance)
key_terms.ذَاتِ الدِّينِ: One who possesses religion/piety (referring to a woman)

ai.seo_question: What is the primary criterion for choosing a spouse according to the Prophet's advice in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophetic tradition of prioritizing spiritual piety (dhāt al-dīn) over worldly status in marriage, a core criterion in Shia jurisprudence for ensuring a righteous household. The concluding phrase 'taribat yadaka' (may your hand be enriched) underscores that choosing a pious spouse leads to both spiritual and material prosperity, reinforcing the merit of those who marry for religion as opposed to wealth or beauty.
